setting_and_country.quote: The educational framework was initiated at a university hospital in Denmark in September 2011.

design.value: Qualitative: focus group interviews (descriptive phenomenological approach)
design.quote: The study draws on a qualitative study design using focus group interviews

participants.value: 14 junior scientists: 7 PhD students, 5 scholarship (medical) students, 2 clinical research nurses
participants.quote: The participants were 7 PhD students, 5 scholarship students and 2 clinical research nurses

group_format.value: Writing for publication: kick-off seminar, then three courses over 10 months, each with 4 weeks of outline preparation, a one-day retreat to dictate a manuscript draft and 8 weeks of revision, supported by supervisor-led writing teams
group_format.quote: a 4-week preparation period for creating a structured manuscript outline, a one-day retreat for dictating a scientific manuscript draft

comparison.quote: We used purposive sampling [17], including all participants in the first of the three Writing for publication courses.

confidence_self_efficacy.value: Not measured; the authors suggest the approach may encourage confidence in writing skills
confidence_self_efficacy.quote: to encourage participants’ confidence in writing skills and raise publication rates

other_writing_outcomes.value: Every participant dictated a full manuscript draft in one session (1.5–7 h); three articles each submitted; flow-like states; writing teams valued for feedback, some felt unable to give feedback
other_writing_outcomes.quote: they all dictated a full manuscript draft in one single session lasting 1.5–7.0 hours

notes: The writing teams were supervisor-led, so this is peer support with a supervisor rather than a purely peer group; the main method is dictation.
